content.text:
**Merged and landed.** PR #547 squashed to `main` as `f0eff57`, local `main` synced (it needed a `--hard` reset — the container's clone is shallow, so the stale local ref looked like it had unique commits it didn't), #548 auto-closed, and the conversation captured to `conversation-logs` as 85 entries.

Answering your question:

## The exit-11 diagnosis

**Symptom:** a dispatch issue that had already been claimed, run, and closed produced a *second* executor session. That session ran step 1, found the issue no longer carried a ready label, exited `11`, and stopped without writing anything — which is exactly correct behavior.

**Ruled out — the repo's own code.** Every label write in the scheduler is guarded: `rearmDispatchIssues` requires open + ready-label-present + no `agent-running` + no `needs-human` + zero comments + >20 min old, and a converged dispatch fails four of those. Stale escalation and dead-claim recovery are open-only too. Confirmed live: GitHub's cron drifted so the scheduler ran at 04:52 then not again until 08:10, and issue #537 was claimed 04:55 and closed 05:07 — no scheduler run existed in that window at all.

**So the extra trigger came from the Routine side**, and both candidates are about the Routine's **label filter**:

- **A — the executor's own claim re-fires its own Routine.** Step 2 swaps `ready-for-agent` → `agent-running`. That add is itself an `issues.labeled` event on the same issue. If the filter isn't narrowed to `ready-for-agent`, the session's own claim starts a second session.
- **B — two Routines on one repo event.** Claudinite is the only member with two label-wired Routines (self + fleet). If the fleet one's filter is missing or overlapping, one event starts two sessions.

**Discriminator:** the phantom's start time. Fires ~1 min after the dispatch was filed (claim time) → A. Fires at the same instant as the dispatch → B.

**Cost so far: zero.** Exit 11 plus the claim protocol absorbed it silently. That's also why it went unnoticed.

## What #422 is

[#422 — "Wire the canon's executor Routines (self + fleet) — last step of the scheduler cutover"](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/422), open since 24 July. It records that both Routines were created as *poke-only bases* through the trigger API, and lists what still has to be finished by hand in settings: attach the GitHub connector, set the trigger to the label event, **set the label filter** (`ready-for-agent` / `ready-for-agent-fleet`), model `sonnet`, and the right sources. It ends "Close this once both Routines are wired."

So #422 is literally the tracking issue for the unset label filter that is the leading suspect. And the change just merged adds one item to it: since scope now comes from the launcher prompt, the **fleet Routine's prompt must carry `fleet`** — previously the fleet session guessed `self` and recovered only because the exit-11 error text hinted at it.

Say "post it" and I'll add the diagnosis and that new acceptance item to #422 so it survives this session.

> ✅ **Done and merged** — PR #547 is on `main`, #548 closed, nothing outstanding on the trim.
>
> ⚠️ **Still open (yours, not mine):** [#422](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/422) — the Routine label filters and the fleet Routine's `fleet` prompt are UI-only; I can't set or verify them.
